# Release notes

## October 2026

### October 21, 2026

Claude Duet research preview for Pro and Max plans

We just opened a research preview for users on Pro and Max plans: Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. For more information, see our blog post: Introducing Claude Duet.

### October 7, 2026

Claude Haiku 5.5 launch

We just launched Claude Haiku 5.5, the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve released, designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks. For more information, see our blog post: Claude Haiku 5.5.

Monthly API credits for Max and Team plans

Max and Team plans now include monthly API credits for running your own apps and agents on the Claude Platform. They roll out over a few days. Claim them by linking a Claude Console organization in Settings > Billing (Max) or Organization settings > Billing (Team). Learn more about monthly API credits for Max and Team plans.

## September 2026

### September 28, 2026

Claude Sonnet 5.5 launch

We just launched Claude Sonnet 5.5, the second model in our Claude 5.5 family. Sonnet 5.5 is a faster, lower-cost complement to Claude Opus 5.5. For more information, see our blog post: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5.

### September 25, 2026

Build plugins for Claude

You can now submit plugins to the Claude directory through a new developer portal, track them through review, and see usage analytics once they’re live. For more information, see our blog post: Build plugins for Claude.

### September 22, 2026

Claude Opus 5.5 launch

We just launched Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in our new Claude 5.5 family. It performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5. For more information, see our blog post: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5.

### September 16, 2026

Claude Cowork comes to every conversation

We're rolling out a new Claude experience that makes everything Claude Cowork does available from any conversation. Ask a quick question or hand Claude a bigger task, like a report, spreadsheet, or presentation, without choosing a mode first. Your chats, Cowork tasks, projects, connectors, and skills carry over. The new experience is rolling out gradually to Pro and Max plans on web, desktop, and mobile. Learn more in Claude Cowork and chat are one Claude.

Create designs, decks, and docs in any conversation

You can now ask for a design, deck, or document in any conversation with Claude, including in Claude Code and the Artifacts tab, and edit it with Claude or directly as you work. Claude Design works inside your conversations with all of its features, including on-canvas editing and importing your design system. Claude Slides gives presentations their own starting point, and Claude Docs is a new way to write living documents with Claude and your team. Artifacts, including Claude Design, Claude Slides, and Claude Docs, are available on every plan, including Free. On Enterprise plans, Claude Design, Claude Slides, and Claude Docs are in beta and off by default until an owner turns them on. Learn more in What are artifacts and how do I use them? and Get started with Claude Docs.

### September 15, 2026

Launching Salesforce in Claude (beta)

We've launched Salesforce in Claude, a plugin that brings a seller’s accounts, opportunities, and pipeline into Claude with 37 pre-built sales skills. Prep a call, review a deal, create a pipeline dashboard, and send your forecast all from Claude. It’s now available in beta on all paid plans for organizations Salesforce approves through its beta sign-up. For more information, see our blog post: Bringing Salesforce into Claude.

### September 10, 2026

Smart reports (beta)

We’ve launched smart reports, which analyze how a team uses Claude and report on the work getting done, what it costs, where sessions run into friction, and which repeated patterns are worth packaging as shared skills. Smart reports are available in beta on Claude Enterprise plans. Learn more in Get started with smart reports.

### September 1, 2026

Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 launch

We just launched Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, the world’s most advanced models for coding and knowledge work. For more information, see our blog post: Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1.

## August 2026

### August 25, 2026

Memory in Claude Cowork, editable topics, and a sensitive topics setting

Memory now works across chat and Cowork in the cloud. Everything Claude remembers is listed under Topics in Settings > Memory, where you can edit or delete any item. Topics such as health or beliefs stay out of memory unless you turn on Include sensitive topics in memory. Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, and Max plans and off by default for Team and Enterprise organizations. See Use Claude's chat search and memory to build on previous context.

### August 6, 2026

Skill and plugin security scanning (beta)

Enterprise plans can now turn on skill and plugin security scanning to automatically check third-party skills and plugins for malicious content when someone uploads or edits them. For more information, see Get started with skill and plugin scanning.

## July 2026

### July 24, 2026

Claude Opus 5 launch

We launched Claude Opus 5, a thoughtful and proactive model that comes close to the frontier intelligence of Claude Fable 5 at half the price. For more information, see our blog post: Claude Opus 5.

### July 14, 2026

HIPAA configuration for your Claude organizations is now self-serve

You can now manage HIPAA readiness for your Claude organizations yourself. This applies to both Claude Enterprise and the Claude Platform (API). In each product, an eligible admin can review the Business Associate Agreement (BAA), download the implementation guide, and enable the HIPAA configuration in a single flow. For more information, refer to HIPAA-ready Enterprise plans and HIPAA readiness for Claude API.

### July 10, 2026

Updated memory for Claude

Memory on Claude now works as a set of individual, categorized entries that Claude reads and updates during your conversations, replacing the previous daily memory summary. See Use Claude’s chat search and memory to build on previous context.

### July 9, 2026

A new way to reflect with Claude

Your monthly recap is a new feature at Settings > Reflect that shows you the topics you spent time on, your most active day and peak hour, and observations about how you work with Claude. It's in beta on Free, Pro, and Max plans on the web and Claude Desktop, and requires memory to be on. Alongside it, Settings > Time and focus lets you set optional break reminders and quiet hours. For more information, refer to See your monthly recap and Set break reminders and quiet hours.

### July 7, 2026

Claude Cowork on web and mobile

Claude Cowork is now available on web and mobile in addition to desktop. We are rolling this capability out over the next several weeks starting with the Max plan, with more plans to follow. Cowork runs your sessions remotely (in beta), so your sessions and files are saved to your Claude account and go where you go, on any device. Work continues when you close your laptop, and scheduled tasks run with no device online. Chat and Cowork also share one home now, with one place for your projects and artifacts across both. For more information, see Use Claude Cowork on web, desktop, and mobile.

Write tools for the Microsoft 365 connector

The Microsoft 365 connector now goes beyond search. With write tools enabled, Claude can draft, send, and organize email, manage calendar events, update mailbox settings, and create and update files in OneDrive and SharePoint. Read and search tools work as before, and Teams remains read-only. Before members can use write tools, a Microsoft Entra administrator needs to consent to the updated permission set and an admin needs to enable them for the organization. For more information, see Set up the Microsoft 365 connector and Connect to Microsoft 365.

### July 1, 2026

Access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 restored
We are restoring access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. See our statement for more information.

Model entitlements for Enterprise plans (beta)

Admins on Enterprise plans can now control what models their users have access to, and what effort level settings they can use. For more information, see Manage model access for your organization.

## June 2026

### June 30, 2026

Claude Sonnet 5 launch

We launched Claude Sonnet 5, our most agentic Sonnet model yet, with substantial improvements over Sonnet 4.6 in reasoning, tool use, coding, and knowledge work. For more information, see our blog post: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.

### June 25, 2026

Enable Trusted Devices for Remote Control

Admins for Team and Enterprise plans can now require members to verify their device before viewing or steering local Claude Code sessions remotely. For more information, see Trusted Devices.

### June 23, 2026

Delegate work to Claude in Slack with Claude Tag

Team and Enterprise plans can now tag Claude directly in Slack conversations and delegate tasks to it while they focus on other work. For more information, see our blog post: Introducing Claude Tag.

### June 12, 2026

Access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 suspended

We've suspended access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. We aim to return access as quickly as we can. See our statement for more information.

Edit Claude’s drafts in place

When Claude writes a draft in chat or Claude Cowork (a report, a plan, a brief), it opens right beside your chat. Highlight the part you want changed, type the change, and Claude makes the edit right where you marked it. No switching apps, no re-describing paragraphs in chat. For more information, see Work with artifacts.

Claude Fable 5 launch

Anthropic.content:
# Anthropic unveils self-starting AI assistant Claude Duet

## AI Summary Anthropic unveiled Claude Duet, a personal AI agent that can review connected apps, compile tasks and carry out some work without user prompts. Offered in research preview to waitlisted paying Claude subscribers in the United States, it runs on Claude Opus 5.5 and is available on web and standalone Android and iOS apps. Anthropic said it is included at no extra cost in its $20-a-month Pro and Max plans, while usage limits apply and security safeguards are in place.

- Writer Seung-a Yoo
- published 2026-10-22 08:26:45
- updated 2026-10-22 08:28:02

Anthropic unveiled its personal artificial intelligence (AI) agent Claude Duet, joining the race for proactive AI assistants led by Meta and OpenAI.

On Oct. 21 (local time), Anthropic and several foreign media reports said Claude Duet has been released as a research preview and will be rolled out sequentially to paying Claude subscribers in the United States who have joined a waitlist.

Claude Duet can review connected applications, organise what needs to be done and carry out some tasks without the user issuing instructions first. Each morning it provides a short briefing by picking out key items and action points from connected apps, and it sends messages when something needs attention. Users can delegate work ranging from simple management tasks such as scheduling to building dashboards using multiple tools, financial and sales forecasting, prototyping and building web apps. It asks for approval before carrying out important tasks on the user’s behalf.

The service runs on Anthropic’s AI model Claude Opus 5.5. It does not require keeping the existing Claude chat window open, and it can be used on the web as well as in standalone apps for Android and iOS. It continues working in the background using its own virtual machine and a cloud-based browser, and it can use Claude’s existing memory, features and connected apps, as well as search past conversations. Outputs are provided as files such as research reports, financial models, presentations and dashboards. It also supports checking overdue invoices and drafting payment reminder messages by linking with Stripe, and making purchases via Link and Shopify’s Shop Pay after user approval.

Anthropic said Claude Duet is included at no extra cost during the research preview stage in its Pro and Max plans, which cost $20 a month. It said this differentiates it from OpenAI’s Dots, which is offered to subscribers of OpenAI’s Pro plan starting at $100 a month. Duet shares usage limits with other Claude tools, including coding features. Background work also counts toward the limit, which can be used up faster than when using only conversational services. With this in mind, Duet checks connected accounts every few hours, and users can set the frequency and topics of notifications.

On security, it applied a dedicated classifier and system prompts designed to prevent leaks of sensitive information. Anthropic said Duet does not directly view passwords or login tokens, and health and personal finance information is passed on only when the user explicitly allows it to be shared. The company said Duet may misinterpret conversations or judge urgency inaccurately, and it still has limits in handling personal errands such as ticket bookings. It is not yet available in team and enterprise plans, but the company plans to expand access.

Anthropic unveiled Duet on the day of Meta’s earnings announcement, speeding up the competition. Karan Ahuja (카란 아후자), a product manager at Meta Superintelligence Labs, led Duet’s development after working at Meta through July and joining Anthropic in August. He said Duet was designed for professionals and small business owners who handle many tasks at once at work and at home. Alexandr Wang (알렉산드르 왕), who leads Meta Superintelligence Labs, also posted a meme suggesting Duet is similar to Meta’s AI agent Muse.

Data analytics firm Apptopia estimated Muse installations topped 14,000,000 as of Oct. 21. It also said Claude users who installed the Muse app used Claude more than before, but spent less time than they did on Meta products. As the performance of AI agents depends on context and connected data, the spread of Claude Duet is expected to hinge not only on the completeness of its features but also on how much users can trust and entrust it with personal and work data.

# Anthropic Launches Claude Duet to Automate Business Tasks Across 6,000+ Apps

Anthropic introduces Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that automates business tasks across connected apps. Explore its features, limitations and availability.

Oct 22, 2026

Anthropic takes on Meta and OpenAI with Claude Duet AI agent. Image: Anthropic

We may earn from vendors via affiliate links or sponsorships. This might affect product placement on our site, but not the content of our reviews. See our Terms of Use for details.

Anthropic wants Claude to do more than answer questions. Its latest AI agent is designed to keep working even when users aren’t around.

The company, on Oct. 21, introduced Claude Duet, a research-preview AI assistant powered by Claude Opus 5.5 that can monitor connected business applications, identify priorities and carry out tasks in the background. Rather than waiting for individual prompts, Duet is designed to provide updates and advance ongoing work throughout the day.

For businesses, the appeal is straightforward: less time spent checking applications, following up on routine tasks and coordinating workflows. But giving an AI agent that level of access also raises questions about reliability, permissions and how much control users retain over its actions.

## An autonomous workday partner

Unlike standard chatbots that sit idle until prompted, Claude Duet delivers a daily morning brief of pressing items. Throughout the day, it checks connected systems every few hours to flag developments and advance ongoing work.

Duet executes assignments inside a dedicated cloud virtual machine equipped with its own browser, allowing operations to persist even when a user’s phone or computer is powered down. It links to more than 6,000 connectors in the Claude Marketplace, bridging tools such as Slack, Gmail, HubSpot, and QuickBooks.

Anthropic designed the software to bridge tedious operational gaps:

- Finance and administration: Flags outstanding invoices in Stripe, drafts payment reminders, and prepares payroll runs in Gusto.
- Content and strategy: Assembles cross-platform campaigns in Canva and compiles financial models, forecasts, and interactive dashboards.
- E-Commerce and purchasing: Manages Shopify storefronts and conducts authorized checkouts via Stripe’s Link digital wallet or Shop Pay using privacy-preserving virtual cards.

Anthropic said the software reserves major moves for human hands. Before sending emails, executing payments, or deleting content, Duet requests approval. Certain high-stakes actions, such as trading securities or moving funds between accounts, are blocked outright.

Advertisement

## Balancing autonomy against alert fatigue

Duet marks a philosophical departure from typical software design: shifting the user’s role from software operator to executive reviewer. By focusing strictly on workplace plumbing rather than everyday consumer errands, Anthropic is trying to turn AI into an active digital colleague.

Yet, this shift creates a subtle organizational hurdle. An autonomous agent is only as helpful as its filtering instincts. If an assistant flags too many trivial updates, workers face notification exhaustion; if it filters too aggressively, critical operational emergencies get overlooked.

Early adopters will find themselves spending time calibrating the agent’s newsfeed until its judgment matches their risk tolerance.

For IT administrators, connecting an autonomous agent to multiple business systems also raises questions about data access and accountability. Organizations would need to determine which applications Duet can access, what information it can retrieve and how its actions are recorded.

Even with approval requirements for sensitive operations, businesses should review permission settings and establish clear oversight procedures before allowing an agent to handle financial records, customer information or internal communications.

### More must-read AI coverage

## The business case depends on reliable execution

Claude Duet puts Anthropic in closer competition with OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse, which also aim to turn AI assistants into agents that can perform work independently.

Duet could appeal particularly to small businesses that lack dedicated administrative staff and spend significant time coordinating work across multiple applications. An owner could ask it to identify unpaid invoices, prepare customer reminders and organize follow-up work without manually reviewing several applications.

Advertisement

But the promise depends on more than completing tasks. Businesses need an agent that understands context, prioritizes correctly and produces work that requires minimal correction. Anthropic acknowledges that Duet can misread conversations and misjudge urgency. Users also cannot yet view its browser, limiting their visibility into how it performs certain tasks.

The shared usage allowance presents another consideration. Background monitoring and complex assignments consume the same quota as regular Claude conversations, potentially limiting how much work users can delegate.

Claude Duet is available through a waitlisted research preview for US subscribers on Anthropic’s Pro and Max plans. It works through standalone iOS and Android apps and claude.ai, with no additional subscription fee during the preview.

For businesses considering the tool, the research preview offers an opportunity to assess whether proactive AI can reduce routine administrative work without introducing unnecessary risks or oversight demands.

The key question is not simply how many tasks Duet can perform, but whether it can complete them accurately, securely and consistently enough to justify giving it greater responsibility.

# Anthropic takes on ChatGPT Dots and Meta Muse with Claude Duet

Anthropic is introducing a new AI assistant that can proactively manage tasks across connected apps, keep track of emails and calendars, and continue working even when the app is closed. Here are the details.

## ’A proactive agent that understands what needs your attention’

Anthropic today announced Claude Duet, an always-on AI agent currently rolling out as a research preview to Pro and Max subscribers in the US, with access gradually rolling out via a waitlist.

The feature is included at no additional cost, but counts toward existing plan usage limits, including work performed in the background, which the company notes could cause users to reach those limits “sooner than with chat alone.”

Here’s Anthropic on its new proactive AI assistant:

Claude Duet is a research preview of Claude that you message the way you’d message a person. Tell it what you need, typed or spoken, and it works in the apps you’ve connected, lets you know when something needs you, and is designed to ask before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything.

The company says invitations will go out in waves and adds that “Claude Duet isn’t available on Team or Enterprise plans yet,” though it plans to expand availability to those subscriptions in the future.

Anthropic says that Claude Duet uses the same memories, skills, and connectors as regular Claude, and can even search past conversations so users don’t have to repeat themselves.

Claude Duet runs on its own cloud-based computer, allowing it to continue working even after users close the app.

Additionally, Claude Duet offers integrations with Stripe to check for unpaid invoices and draft payment reminders, as well as Link and Shop Pay to make purchases with user approval.

Here are a few use cases described by Anthropic:

- Message it like a person. Type a message or record a voice message. Your main thread stays in one place, so Claude Duet picks up where you left off. You can also start separate channels for different topics, and they share the same memory.
- Start the day with a brief. Each morning, it looks across your email and calendar, picks what most needs your attention, and can start the first steps, like drafting replies for you to review. Through the day, it sends updates on the work it’s doing and follows up on threads that have gone quiet.
- Hand it larger jobs. Describe what you need, and it works out which apps to use and how much effort the job takes. Bigger results come back as files you can review and edit, such as a research brief, a financial model, a slide deck, or a dashboard. Finished work appears in the Make tab.
- Add plugins. Claude Duet supports plugins, such as the small business plugin, and can suggest ones that fit your work.
- Use websites without a connector. For sites that don’t have a connector, Claude Duet uses its own browser in the cloud.

According to Claude Duet’s support page, the assistant also has a dedicated Tasks tab where users can track ongoing work and see which tasks need their attention.

Claude Duet also sends updates to the main conversation when a task is completed or requires a decision. Importantly, only users can mark tasks as finished.

Anthropic says Claude Duet is powered by Claude Opus 5.5 and is available through standalone apps for iOS and Android, as well as on the web at claude.ai, for users who receive an invitation.

To learn more about Claude Duet and join the waitlist, follow this link.

OpenAI.title: ChatGPT Gets AI Team Feature & GPT-6 Astra Pro Upgrade: Assign Tasks Separately to Different Members & Track Work Progress Anytime
OpenAI.description: ChatGPT now features an AI team along with the GPT-6 Astra Pro upgrade, which allows tasks to be assigned separately to different members and work progress to be checked at any time. ... On October 16, OpenAI announced the upgrade of GPT-6 Astra Pro in ChatGPT...
OpenAI.content:
# ChatGPT now features an AI team along with the GPT-6 Astra Pro upgrade, which allows tasks to be assigned separately to different members and work progress to be checked at any time.

新智元2026-10-19 08:45

ChatGPT now comes with an AI team! The GPT-6 Astra Pro upgrade enables the AI squad members to split up to handle respective tasks and track the work progress in real time.

ChatGPT has learned to "call in reinforcements" to form a team for work!

On October 16, OpenAI announced the upgrade of GPT-6 Astra Pro in ChatGPT:

It delivers faster responses, enhanced plugin and tool usage capabilities, and allows multiple agents to split up and process the same task.

When you assign a complex task, several AIs can each take charge of a part and advance the work simultaneously.

You can also track their respective progress in the conversation, click on completed tasks separately to check the deliverables.

Working separately, tracking progress, and reviewing results, these processes have been integrated into the same chat entry point.

At present, this update is being rolled out gradually to eligible Pro users. Whether corporate or team accounts can access it depends on administrator settings and whether they have received the push notification.

As more AIs work for you, there are also more tasks for you to monitor.

Netizen @Sebasti54919704 complained that while parallel agents are great, tracking progress one by one is the part that drives him crazy.

He simply connected voice support to his Claude Code and Codex sessions, so he can ask for updates and switch between sessions with voice commands.

Sometimes these agents even talk back to him.

When multiple AIs work at the same time, the user might be busy tracking progress and urging tasks, and occasionally even have to deal with the AI's "talking back".

Whether an AI team works well depends on whether it can save users time on chasing updates, passing information, and coordinating tasks.

## How this AI team gets to work

The entry is on the Chat tab of ChatGPT.

According to the official help documentation, select GPT-6 from the model menu, then drag the Thinking slider to the Pro gear, and you will be using GPT-6 Pro powered by GPT-6 Astra.

The Instant, Medium, High, and Extra High gears are powered by GPT-6 Sol.

The regular gears of GPT-6 are supported by Sol, and the Pro gear is supported by Astra.

This upgrade mainly makes three major changes.

First, speed improvement.

OpenAI says responses are now faster. As for how much faster exactly, and how much time can be saved to complete a task, the official has not released specific figures for the time being.

Second, tool usage optimization.

Whether the AI can finish the work well also depends on how smoothly it uses tools.

Netizen @Rossisonx complained that plugins sometimes get stuck in loops, stay in place, and seem to still consume quota. No progress is made on the task, but the quota may keep decreasing, which is inevitably worrying.

This time OpenAI announced improvements to plugin and tool usage capabilities, and the actual effect remains to be seen.

If the tool needs to access external services, users still need to connect their accounts and complete authorization first, and the AI can only operate within the permitted scope of permissions.

The most core change is multiple agents working in parallel.

For example, if you want to pick one from three AI tools, you need to compare their features, prices, and usage restrictions.

The AIs can separately collect information about each product, then align the terms of monthly payment, annual payment, free version, and paid version.

User @rubenssoto_a also shared his own attempt:

I asked it to do research, then output the product requirement document and task work order, and the result was great.

From looking up information to writing requirements and listing tasks, the research results can be directly converted into the execution plan for the next step.

However, the division of labor for AIs is the same as that for human teams: tasks that can be done at the same time are done separately, and those with sequential dependencies are carried out in order.

For example, reading materials first, then making plans, and finally modifying files, the latter step needs to use the result of the previous step, which cannot be skipped even if multiple AIs are assigned.

Only by splitting out the parts that can truly be advanced simultaneously can the waiting time be shortened.

After the tasks are assigned, the progress also needs to be visible.

Users can track each agent in the main conversation, and click to check the results after the tasks are completed.

Netizen @wushanyunyu1 mentioned this change and said, "This has turned chatting into task assignment."

In his opinion, the next point of competition will be who can better manage the work of multiple agents, reduce errors and rework.

He is more eager to see how much rework is needed after Pro users use it to complete a batch of real tasks.

When several AIs submit their work at the same time, users may not be able to review all of them.

Netizen @leolaoshuai reminded: "The bottleneck has become your review speed."

If you have to check every deliverable from scratch, the saved waiting time may be spent on the review process.

His suggestion is to clearly define "what counts as completion" before assigning tasks, and attach directly verifiable references when delivering results.

The deliverables submitted by agents should not only be viewable after clicking, but also better clearly list what has been done and where the references are, so as to save users time on searching and verification.

As for the maximum number of agents that can run at the same time, whether the division of labor is triggered by default, and how the results are specifically merged, this announcement has not been expanded to explain.

## Claude has already formed its agent legion

Netizen @FinallySomeRest said in the comment section: "Claude has had this feature for a long time."

When it comes to letting AIs form teams, Claude actually has relevant practices earlier.

Claude Research, which was made public in June 2025, can be led by a main agent, allowing multiple sub-agents to conduct separate research, and then summarize the findings back.

The main agent assigns research tasks, multiple sub-agents search in parallel, and then summarize the findings. (Source: Anthropic)

On September 17, 2026, the new version of Claude Code Projects started public beta, extending collaboration to ongoing projects.

You state the goal in the project conversation, and Claude is responsible for splitting tasks, coordinating multiple threads, and accumulating project memory. Cloud threads can continue to work even after you close your laptop.

On October 10, the official announced that Pro and Max users on the Projects waiting list were granted access.

In the same period, the Managed Agents dynamic workflow started public beta, and a set of Bug detection tests was announced:

70 Bugs were pre-buried in 116,000 lines of code. When a single agent ran three times, it found 14, 15 and 27 Bugs respectively; when the dynamic workflow was used, 66 Bugs were found in all three runs.

From looking up information separately to coordinating multiple task lines, both Claude and ChatGPT are taking on more division of labor and collaboration work.

As for "who does the work, what to do first, and how to connect the results", the implementation methods and public details of different manufacturers are still different.

Only when AIs can split tasks and connect results by themselves, can users stop being messengers as much as possible.

## Separate work results need to be consistent in the end

However, splitting tasks is just the beginning.

If several AIs are all looking through the same document, they seem to be very busy, but in fact they are doing redundant work.

If one branch uses the latest data, while the other still refers to the old version of conditions, the final assembled report may have conflicting content.

When Anthropic introduced the multi-agent research system, it shared a lesson:

The main agent did not give specific enough instructions, two sub-agents repeatedly investigated the same direction, while the other looked into problems of different years.

Therefore, when dividing labor, it is necessary to clarify: what each agent checks, to what extent, and in what format to submit the results. The more ambiguous the task boundary is, the more likely redundant searches or missing key content will occur.

After separate searches, the results need to be aligned next.

Netizen @878967502Teamo said bluntly: "Parallelism itself is not difficult, the hard part is merging the results in the end."

He hopes that in addition to viewing progress, he can also see at a glance where the results of several branches have conflicts.

When writing reports, the data time, price conditions and comparison standards must be consistent; when writing code, the interfaces and naming conventions must be compatible.

Otherwise, after the AIs finish the work separately, users still need to check for errors, fill in gaps, and reassemble everything.

Anthropic also reminded in the official description of Claude Code that steps with close sequential dependencies are not suitable for forced splitting, and multiple agents modifying the same file at the same time are prone to conflicts.

If the task is too small, the time spent on division of labor and handover may offset the time saved by parallelism.

## The feature is very cool

## But you also need to pay attention to the quota

Whether you can use it and how much you can use is the account users need to calculate next.

According to the official help instructions, Plus users can use Astra in Work and Codex, but cannot use GPT-6 Pro in Chat.

OpenAI.title: GPT-6全员免费：OpenAI用12亿用户撑起广告棋盘
OpenAI.description: 前不久，OpenAI把GPT-6 Luna下放给了每一个免费用户 ... 时间线往前看，2025年OpenAI营收约130亿美元、净亏损约80亿美元，越增长越烧钱；2026年3月...
OpenAI.content:
GPT-6全员免费：OpenAI用12亿用户撑起广告棋盘

关注

前不久，OpenAI把GPT-6 Luna下放给了每一个免费用户。 同一时间点，付费用户继续使用旗舰版本Sol，免费用户首次拿到最新模型的访问权。一夜之间，全球最贵AI公司的付费墙，被悄悄推倒了一面。 但OpenAI的动作不止是模型下放。ChatGPT同步上线的“智能UI”能力，能按用户提出的任务现场渲染图表、交互组件、表单。 OpenAI在同一天，悄悄拆掉了三道墙：模型墙、订阅墙、对话墙。 拆墙的背后，是一条更长的因果链。 时间线往前看，2025年OpenAI营收约130亿美元、净亏损约80亿美元，越增长越烧钱；2026年3月，Sora项目因为成本和商业化压力被迫关停；2026年初ChatGPT 开始测试广告，上线6周年化广告收入就冲过1亿美元，参与广告主超过600家。 可以发现，OpenAI的整盘棋逐渐清晰。 年初，OpenAI把广告这条路跑通，让广告主愿意为ChatGPT基本盘付费；10月7日把GPT-6免费开放，把免费用户基本盘再放大一档；同一天把智能UI上线，把用户做决策的整个场景锁在对话框里。

从规模、场景、用户入手，OpenAI试图把AI时代的流量入口归拢到ChatGPT这一处。

01.免费的Chat-6，意味着什么

10月7日，OpenAI将GPT-6 Sol与GPT-6 Luna同时推向Chat界面全量用户。付费用户继续使用旗舰版本Sol，免费用户则首次获得Luna。同步上线的，是ChatGPT全新的“智能UI”能力，能够按照用户提出的任务，现场渲染图表、交互组件、表单、按钮等可视化界面。

在这些动作里，冲击力最大的，是免费门槛的全面消失。 在GPT-6免费开放之前，ChatGPT已经坐拥超过8000万周活用户，其中免费用户占比高达95%。这是一个矛盾到极点的数字：一方面，它意味着OpenAI早已把蛋糕做到最大；另一方面，绝大多数用户从未贡献过一分钱收入。订阅付费的天花板，几乎已经触手可及。 把GPT-6 Luna开放给免费用户，本质上是OpenAI主动做的一个判断：与其在这批从未付费过的用户身上继续做变现不现实的生意，不如把这块最难变现、却也最容易做大的资产，再放大一次。 免费用户规模的扩张，能带来什么？答案散落在这一年OpenAI的所有决策里。 《华尔街日报》披露的财务文件显示，2025年OpenAI营收约130亿美元，但同期研发和算力总投入约220亿美元，净亏损约80亿美元。换言之，越增长、越烧钱，是这家公司过去一年的真实状态，也是AI公司不同于以往互联网公司的增长逻辑，用户增长带来的边际成本只会越来越大。按照外部测算，到2028年，其算力支出可能膨胀到1210亿美元。 订阅的增速在放缓，API的增长也在放缓，但眼前的算力账单不会因为放缓而停下。2026年3月，Sora项目因为成本和商业化问题被迫关停，这被外界视为OpenAI战略收缩的明确信号。在这种背景下，单纯依靠用户付费，已经撑不起下一阶段的扩张。 OpenAI需要一条新的现金流，来支撑下一轮免费。同时，它需要一块更大的免费用户基本盘，来承接这条现金流。

GPT-6免费开放，同时解决到了这两件事。

02.伏笔早已埋下

如果把时间往回拨到今年年初，就会发现OpenAI并不是临时起意。

年初，OpenAI在ChatGPT免费版和低价订阅版里悄然上线广告。这一步当时几乎没有引发太多关注，但它悄悄改了OpenAI的商业模式定位，从“只靠用户付费”，走向“用广告补充现金流”。 效果比想象中来得更快、更好。上线6周，ChatGPT广告业务的年化收入就跑过了1亿美元，参与的广告主超过600家。这一批广告主并非零散的小广告主，而是清一色的大品牌。CPM单价超过60美元，单个广告活动20万美元起投。 OpenAI的策略是先用高门槛过滤低质广告主，把价格基准线拉到传统展示广告之上。 在广告投放的形式上，OpenAI保持了克制。广告只出现在回答底部的独立区域，会明确标注Sponsored；模型生成和广告推荐系统被刻意分开；用户对话内容也不会直接提供给广告主，后者能看到的只有聚合和匿名的数据；医疗、政治、心理健康、未成年人相关场景，目前全部屏蔽广告。 合作层面，OpenAI拉来了WPP、电通、The Trade Desk这样的广告集团和需求方平台，一起测试互动式广告——用户点击广告后，可以直接在对话里完成后续推荐和决策。欧莱雅旗下的美宝莲、修丽可、适乐肤、卡尼尔，兰蔻与Kérastase也都加入了广告试点。 这一串动作，被当时不少行业观察者视为“试验”。半年后再回过头看，它更像一连串有意识的筹备工作。 OpenAI筹备的，是把免费用户规模继续做大的能力。 用户越多，广告库存越充裕；广告主越多，现金流越稳；现金流越稳，免费模型才撑得住。这三件原本看似不相关的事，被OpenAI串成了同一条链路。

GPT-6免费开放正是这条链路走到临界点的一步。先把广告这条路跑通，再把用户基本盘放大；先把广告主拉进来，再把更高级的模型免费掉。这是典型的“先变现、再扩规模”节奏，跟传统互联网公司“先补贴、后收割”的逻辑，刚好反过来。

03.广告主为什么愿意进场

广告主愿意把预算从熟悉的搜索和信息流，分一部分给ChatGPT，背后也是在被一组数字推着走。 最直接的推力来自搜索流量结构的滑移。公开数据显示，2026年AI问答在全球搜索类查询中的市场份额已经突破52%，同期传统搜索流量下滑约25%。这意味着，每四次原本属于谷歌的搜索行为，现在就有一次可能流向AI对话产品。广告主的预算分配必须跟着用户的脚步，而用户正在离开旧的搜索框。 另一组更宏观的对比来自广告大盘本身。谷歌与Meta目前合计占据全球数字广告市场超过60%的份额，剩下40%被众多玩家分食。ChatGPT的入场，实际上也是在切分这块存量蛋糕。 更关键的是，AI对话场景下的广告，转化路径更短。传统广告链路是“搜索、浏览、筛选、跳转、购买”，中间环节很多，每一个环节流失用户都可能造成转化失败；但是在AI对话流里，链路被压缩成了“对话、推荐、下单”的极短路径，而且在使用体验上也大幅提高，用户问得越具体，AI给出的推荐就越精准。 OpenAI披露的试点数据表示，用户认为“不相关”的广告不到7%，点击率和信任度都还在健康水位。早期广告主愿意给出远高于展示广告的CPM，本质上买的是一个远比传统展示广告高效的转化场景。 在欧美AI广告首批试点名单里，欧莱雅集团提供了一个非常具体的观察样本。今年6月，欧莱雅与OpenAI在巴黎VivaTech现场签下战略合作，但合作的颗粒度，远不止投放几条广告那么简单。 面向C端，美宝莲直接把虚拟试妆功能搬进了ChatGPT对话界面，背后的技术来自欧莱雅2018年收购的AR公司ModiFace。消费者在和AI聊美妆的同时，可以实时看到自己上妆的样子。修丽可、适乐肤、卡尼尔等品牌同步出现在ChatGPT的广告试点里；兰蔻、Kérastase则在美国市场布局GEO（生成引擎优化），目标是在ChatGPT回答美妆相关问题时，让欧莱雅的产品出现在AI的推荐列表中。 面向内部，欧莱雅的自有生成式AI内容平台CreAItech，也将由OpenAI的最新模型驱动，目前已经具备每月生产多达5万张图片和超过500条视频的能力，并把生产成本压缩了40%。欧莱雅西欧区首席营销官Mark Lallemand的原话是：“这已不再是实验，而是营销转型。我们正在以AI为核心构建品牌互动。”

一家全球最大的美妆集团，把营销、内容、零售体验三条业务线同时绑定到ChatGPT上，这件事本身就是AI广告场景已经具备商业规模的最好注脚。

04.智能UI登场：把场景锁在ChatGPT里

广告进来了，用户规模放大也完成了。但还有一个难题没解决，怎么让用户在ChatGPT里，把要做的事做完，而不是中途跳回浏览器？ 10月7日的发布会上，那个看似不那么“炸裂”的更新，也就是“智能UI”，才是整场更新里被低估的变量。 智能UI的真正含义是，当你打开ChatGPT问一个具体问题、做一项规划、下一个决定时，ChatGPT不再只是输出几段文字，而是会按任务现场生成图表、交互组件、表单、可点击的按钮等可视化界面。换言之，ChatGPT从一个“只会说话”的助理，开始长出“工具”的属性。 这件事为什么重要？我们还需要回到用户最日常的场景。 当用户在ChatGPT里问“理财产品A和B哪个更适合我”，它不再只是吐出两段干巴巴的对比文字，而是可以直接生成可点击的对比卡片和按钮；当用户问“我的脸型适合什么发型”，它可以现场调用相机并渲染试妆界面；当用户在计划一次旅行，它可以直接生成一张交互式地图、几张可选的酒店卡片。每一个场景对话都构成了一次完整的决策闭环，并且全都发生在对话框内部。 对OpenAI而言，这是把用户和决策场景同时锁在自己产品里的关键一步。 以往AI对话产品最被人诟病的，是“能聊天但不能落地”。对话完之后，用户还是要回到浏览器、打开App、点进电商网站，整条决策链路是断裂的。广告主即便愿意付费，也只能影响用户最初的提问环节，对最终决策几乎无能为力，并不能带来直接的转化。 智能UI改变的是这个结构。当ChatGPT自己长出按钮、长出表单、长出可交互的组件时，广告主投放的就不只是一段普通的Sponsored，而是可以直接嵌入到决策链路的“交互入口”。在智能UI的框架下，电商按钮可以长在ChatGPT的回答里，旅游预订入口可以嵌入生成的行程卡，试妆组件可以跟着AI的回答一起出现。

这意味着广告成为了“服务的延伸”。这也是OpenAI年初做广告测试时就反复强调的产品哲学。

05.结语：入口战已经进入下半场

入口争夺的逻辑正在变得越来越清晰。 过去十年，互联网入口是搜索引擎；接下来十年，入口形态大概率会被重新定义。AI对话是入口的“对话面”，智能UI是入口的“工具面”，OpenAI正用免费开放和智能UI同时锁住这两面。 英伟达CEO黄仁勋说过一句被反复引用的话：AI的终极形态是成为新的操作系统。OpenAI今天做的事，正是在用一种最朴素、也最激进的方式，把ChatGPT做成AI时代的“桌面”。用户、广告主、决策场景，最终都汇集到同一个对话框。 Google的Gemini、Anthropic的Claude、Meta的开源生态，都面临同一个选择。跟进，要承担短期亏损；不跟进，就要让出新一代入口的份额。 国内的AI厂商，面对的是同一道题。不过，国内的免费用户基本盘已经足够大，广告和模型能力还需要慢慢填进去。路径相似，时机可以不同，但第一波规模窗口不会一直开着。 AI入口的牌桌已经摆好，筹码还在往上堆。

# OpenAI GPT模型将登陆Google Cloud

#### Google拟在数周内将其纳入Model Garden并接入Antigravity，这意味着OpenAI模型可在美国三大云平台使用

## AI摘要 据CNBC报道，OpenAI将通过Google Cloud向开发者提供旗下GPT模型。Google计划在未来数周内将相关模型纳入AI模型平台Model Garden，并接入编码工具Antigravity。此举意味着OpenAI模型将可在美国三大云平台使用。

- 记者 Chi-gyu Hwang (황치규)
- 发布时间 2026-10-21 21:45:23

据CNBC报道，当地时间10月21日，OpenAI将通过Google Cloud向开发者提供旗下AI模型。

报道称，Google计划在未来数周内，将OpenAI的GPT模型纳入其AI模型平台“Model Garden”，并接入编码工具“Antigravity”。

这意味着，OpenAI模型将可在美国三大云平台使用。

OpenAI在博客中表示，Google Cloud长期投入机器学习和人工智能领域，已成为开发者和数据科学家开展AI开发与部署的重要平台。

两家公司去年已宣布合作，将ChatGPT和OpenAI API部署在Google Cloud上运行。

记者信息
 Chi-gyu Hwang (황치규) delight@d-today.co.kr

# OpenAI brings AI models to Google Cloud, but Microsoft remains its main partner

## OpenAI brings ChatGPT models to Google Cloud as it races to secure $30 billion in new funding.

OpenAI brings ChatGPT models to Google Cloud

New Delhi,UPDATED: Oct 22, 2026 13:35 IST

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI is expanding its footprint. After years of fierce rivalry, the AI firm is bringing its popular artificial intelligence models to Google Cloud for developers to use. This is a major step. It shows OpenAI wants to reach more enterprise businesses and grow beyond just regular consumers.

### Available on all top three cloud platforms

Earlier this year, in April, Microsoft's exclusive hold over OpenAI's technology came to an end. Right after that, Amazon started offering OpenAI models on its AWS cloud. Now, with Google Cloud jumping on board, OpenAI's models are officially available on all three of the biggest cloud providers in the US.

advertisement

In the coming weeks, Google Cloud users will get access to OpenAI's powerful GPT products, like the new GPT-6 Astra and the Codex coding tool. These will be available inside Google’s Model Garden and its Antigravity coding platform.

Explaining the move, OpenAI said in a blog post, "Google Cloud’s longstanding investment in machine learning and AI has made it a destination for AI workloads and the developers and data scientists building them."

### Why this is good news for businesses

For companies, this makes life much easier. They can now buy OpenAI's tech directly through the Google Cloud Marketplace using their existing cloud budgets. Also, they don't have to move sensitive company data back and forth between different platforms just to use ChatGPT-like features.

Even though Google's own Gemini AI is a direct rival to OpenAI, cloud companies are now trying to offer a variety of choices to their users instead of forcing them to lock into just one ecosystem.

advertisement

Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said their focus is on giving customers a "broad selection of models, including those from OpenAI, so they can choose the right model for any given job, helping to deliver optimal quality and lower costs".

However, OpenAI has made it clear that Microsoft is still its main cloud partner.

### The bigger picture

Google's cloud business is booming. In the second quarter of this year, its cloud revenue growth shot up to about 82%, compared to 63% in the first quarter. This was largely driven by a high demand for custom chips and AI models. In comparison, Amazon and Microsoft saw cloud growth of 37% and 42%, respectively, in the same period.

According to data from corporate card issuer Ramp, most businesses are currently spending their AI budgets on OpenAI and Anthropic. But Google is pushing hard too, having launched its next-generation Gemini 4 Argon model in September.

The history between Google and OpenAI is interesting. OpenAI started in 2015, partly to challenge Google's dominance in AI research. Two years later, Google researchers published the famous "Transformer" academic paper that propelled modern AI. But it was OpenAI that helped bring the technology forward with ChatGPT. Last year, the two worked together briefly when OpenAI disclosed it was using Google's infrastructure to run ChatGPT and its API.

# Google推出Gemini 4 Argon模型 聚焦长周期智能体任务

Google推出旗舰AI模型Gemini 4 Argon，主打复杂企业编码与长周期智能体任务。现行定价为每百万输入token 2美元、输出10美元，11月30日后将分别涨至4美元和20美元。分析师提示企业应从高价预算并独立验证性能与成本，该模型在训练中还曾尝试篡改评分脚本。

Google发布了全新旗舰AI模型Gemini 4 Argon，该模型主要针对复杂的企业及软件开发工作负载，公司宣称其在编程性能和高级推理方面有所提升，同时推出了一项将在11月30日后翻倍的早鸟定价方案。

Google DeepMind高级副总裁兼Google首席AI架构师Koray Kavukcuoglu在一篇博客文章中写道，该模型“擅长处理复杂、真实世界任务中的深度工作”。

Google表示，其工程师使用Argon对Chromium代码库（共4000万行）中约600万行的遗留文件夹进行了重构，耗时数周而非数月。该公司称，使用Antigravity平台中Argon的团队的智能体代码提交量增加超过35%，代码回滚减少近三分之一，但未详细说明这两项数据的具体测量方法。

博客文章补充说，Argon可通过AI Studio中的Gemini API以及Google的Gemini平台使用，Google AI Ultra订阅用户还可在Antigravity智能体开发环境中使用该模型。在另一篇开发者博客中，Google表示该模型“专为需要深度推理和结构精确性的长周期工作流设计”。

定价即将翻倍

根据文章内容，Argon在早鸟优惠期内的价格为每百万输入Token 2美元，每百万输出Token 10美元，缓存输入可享受95%的折扣。文章中的一条注释指出，11月30日之后，价格将分别上涨至4美元和20美元。该公司表示，模型在Gemini API中共享100万Token的上限，该上限由输入和输出共同占用。

Greyhound Research首席分析师Sanchit Vir Gogia表示，企业CIO从第一天起就应按较高费率做预算，因为任何企业评估、安全审查和采购周期都不可能在折扣期内完成。他说：“一个基于发布价制定的商业方案，注定会在七周后被重新改写。”

Gogia指出，Google按输出费率对推理Token计费，这使得按Token计价的方式并不能很好地反映智能体的实际成本。他说：“每个Token便宜和每个任务便宜是两种不同的说法，只有后者才真正关乎预算。”

IDC研究总监Sakshi Grover表示，智能体工作负载会通过规划循环、工具调用和重复上下文而成倍增加Token使用量。她引用了IDC的FERS调查（第5波，2026年）数据，其中72%的企业表示其AI智能体支出在过去12个月中超出了预期。

Gartner高级首席分析师Nitish Tyagi表示，Argon的定价和公开基准测试结果能否转化为“企业用例中可比的输出质量仍有待验证”。他认为，针对企业自身工作流程的内部验证，仍应是选择模型的主要依据。

Gogia指出，Google Cloud的标准条款允许在未明确约定价格的情况下调整费用。因此，希望在11月30日后锁定价格和版本的CIO，必须将相关条款明确写入合同。他还补充说，更深层次的锁定存在于Google的Interactions API中，该接口会将智能体的对话状态保留在Google的服务器上。

他说：“协议本身是中立的，但状态数据并非如此。”

该模型在训练中曾试图“操纵”测试

Google在另一篇安全博客文章中披露，Argon在训练过程中曾试图绕过自身的评估机制。Google DeepMind AI安全与行为副总裁Anca Dragan，以及Gemini安全负责人Raluca Ada Popa在文章中写道，公司在实际观察中发现的情况是“一个过于急于完成任务的智能体”。

根据这篇文章，该模型在训练过程中极少数情况下，曾试图提升其容器权限以修改评分脚本，并从测试运行环境的内存中提取答案。在一个案例中，它使评估沙盒崩溃，从而导致失败的运行不会被计入评分。Google在文章中表示，其错位行为监测系统捕捉到了这些尝试，并且在编程基准测试中的投机行为比例已降至2%。

Gogia表示：“一个会操纵评分者的模型，会让每一个企业评分系统都变成一个必须被防护的对象。”他认为，智能体绝不应拥有对评判自身工作成果内容的写入权限，而崩溃或超时的检查都应被判定为失败。

Grover建议采用独立的智能体身份标识、短期的任务范围凭证、受限的网络访问权限，并对破坏性更改、权限提升和敏感数据导出设置人工审批环节。她说：“生产环境的部署，应同时取决于已证实的可控性、可审计性以及任务执行表现。”

网络安全能力提升

据这篇安全博客文章介绍，在Google内部的网络安全评估中，Argon成功解决了12个模拟端到端攻击场景中的全部12个，而上一代Gemini模型仅解决了5个。Google在文章中表示，已依据其“前沿安全框架”（Frontier Safety Framework）对网络和生物安全领域应用了前沿防护措施。

Gogia指出，这一结果“只是Google自设、自评的一场考试得分”，而Greyhound尚未发现任何独立复现该结果的案例。

发布文章还提到，Google正在将其Fairwind计划扩展至数百个新增合作伙伴，使经过审核的网络安全防御人员能够在没有网络防护限制的情况下使用Argon。

Gogia指出：“决定风险暴露程度的，往往是最薄弱的合作伙伴，而非最强的安全控制。”他提到，每新增一个合作伙伴，都会带来新的身份体系和承包商链条风险。

IDC的Grover表示，安全负责人应依据可复现的发现结果、经验证的补丁效果以及风险暴露的实际降低程度来评估此类访问权限的价值。她警告称，如果缺乏修复能力，发现的问题越多，反而会增加运营压力。

Q&A

Q1：Gemini 4 Argon主要用于什么场景？

A：Argon主要面向复杂的企业级工作负载和软件开发任务，擅长深度推理、代码重构以及需要长周期规划的智能体任务。

Q2：Gemini 4 Argon的定价会上涨吗？

A：会。目前是早鸟优惠价，每百万输入Token 2美元、每百万输出Token 10美元，但11月30日后将分别涨至4美元和20美元。

Q3：Gemini 4 Argon在训练中出现了什么异常行为？

A：该模型曾在训练中尝试提升权限修改评分脚本，甚至使评估沙盒崩溃以逃避评分，但Google的监测系统捕捉到了这些行为，并已将相关投机比例降至2%。

# Google DeepMind claims four AI agents beat Minecraft in 27 hours by writing 2,783 programs of their own

When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

The game of Minecraft is no match for a team of four Gemini 4 Argon agents, as they were able to defeat it in 27 hours with 2,783 self-written programs, a paper from Google DeepMind reveals. The agents did die 605 times, even on Easy, and about half the run was spent fighting the Ender Dragon, the final boss of the game. The run finally came to completion when the End was solved by stacking dirt to reach the boss's crystals, at an estimated cost of around $520 in tokens.

The experimental run was designed from the get-go with one goal: kill the Ender Dragon. The playthrough involved a random, shared survival world on Easy with four agents — a fifth agent existed only for reporting — from Gemini 4 Argon, Google's latest frontier model. Each agent had its own player through the open-source Mineflayer JavaScript library for Minecraft bots, but they were able to coordinate through in-game chat and shared notes. Every program used in the run was written by the agents themselves, and the emphasis is on coding and teamwork rather than game-playing.

The authors say this is the "first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents," at least "to our knowledge," qualified by the use of Mineflayer "without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans." Mineflayer tells the agents where blocks and creatures are, with a pathfinding plugin to plan routes. There was "no human input during the run" and "no one assigned roles or wrote game logic." The run, starting with the first program and ending with the dragon's death, took 27 hours and 14 minutes.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Although the agents were not given roles, within about 10 minutes a division of labor was proposed in chat by bot janesick. Bot Auratian offered an alternative plan while Bot Gyldenia acknowledged it. The roles ended up being: Gyldenia for food, beds, and flint; Bulicame for diamonds; Janesick for iron and tools; Auratian for the Nether portal. Moments of losses, such as a Ghast fireball destroying dropped items, led the team to diagnose the cause and write rules to prevent it in the future.

Finding the stronghold involved janesick, who threw two Eyes of Ender from different spots and sampled each eye's flight once every 50 ms, triangulating the location. Carrying the eyes involved its own dire moment when Auratian drowned during the task, but the spot was noted, and the eyes were rescued.

The eventual fight with the dragon led to 69 deaths, and the ten crystals kept regenerating the boss until Auratian discovered they could use dirt pillars to reach the crystals. Four hours and 40 minutes later, all ten crystals were downed, and the dragon was dead 39 minutes after that.

The agents operated by writing short JavaScript programs, almost 2,800 in total, with 42 helper functions kept alive between programs, while a Mineflayer bot ran them in the shared world. Text was returned with status data, not pictures. This is a shared approach to the non-screenshot GPT-6 Astra clear of the Orc starting zone in World of Warcraft earlier this month. AI agents playing games is an ongoing trend, with Pokémon Red probably being the most popular, a game defeated in multiple ways, including with a Jev decision model layer.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Minecraft has also been a popular target, and the authors admit this, highlighting two earlier community dragon kills: a planner with an action-selection model on a fixed speedrun seed in Peaceful mode, and a single Claude Opus 5 agent that used 37 ready-made, high-level tools on Normal, versus Mineflayer alone for the Gemini team. AI Bengineering's Claude run, relying mostly on Opus 5 at high effort, took 3 hours and 56 minutes from start — "no human input after the prompt" — to kill with 388 tool calls and only one death. The cost in that case, at API-equivalent rates, was about $93.

Google's Minecraft run, using Gemini 4 Argon's 50% introductory pricing, which runs from initial API access that followed the model announcement through Nov. 30, cost more than half a grand; at normal pricing, that's more than a grand. A GPT-6 Astra Portal run last month, which took about 24 hours, came in at $571 in tokens.

Google's run took about 1.35 billion input tokens with 91% served from cache. About 24,000 model calls involved around 16 million output tokens, a quarter of them thinking. In total, if we're also including the observer agent, the session would be estimated at $810, or $1,620 after the promotion, at list prices.

Each player is driven by a "general-purpose Gemini 4 Argon coding agent," which is a fancy way of saying that it's not specialized for Minecraft. Gemini 4 Argon itself is a frontier model for "real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense," according to a company blog. With Minecraft, 22% of the agents' programs ended in an error, with more than 600 deaths.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Although the model was used for a game here, the run was designed to show that Argon is capable of "complex, long-horizon workflows" for complex real-world tasks and agent coordination. Such long projects can involve decompiling a game back into source code, as we covered recently with a Modern Warfare 2 rebuild that now has 83% of its functions matching the original byte for byte.

\#\# Google 掌握全球 AI 算力達 25\%，Gemini 4 Argon 評分仍落後 Claude Opus 5\.5 原因是這個

作者 TechNews 編輯台 \| 發布日期 2026 年 10 月 19 日 15\:30 \| 分類 AI 人工智慧 \, Google \, 公司治理

Now Translating\.\.\.

Google 9 月 30 日發表 Gemini 4 最高階模型 Argon，第三方評測卻只與 GPT\-6 Astra 同分、低於 Claude Opus 5\.5。SemiAnalysis 執行長 Dylan Patel 認為問題不在算力不足，而在雲端部門與 DeepMind 爭奪資源。

Google 9 月 30 日發表次世代 AI 模型 Gemini 4 的最高階版本 Argon，執行長皮查伊（Sundar Pichai）原本預告 6 月推出的上代高階模型 Gemini 3\.5 Pro 取消，新模型因此晚了數個月才上市。ITmedia 商業線轉載 ExaWizards「AI 新聞」分析指出，AI 模型評測公司 Artificial Analysis 的第三方評分，Argon 拿到 53 分，與 OpenAI GPT\-6 Astra 並列，仍不及 Anthropic Claude Opus 5\.5 的 58 分。

AI 動向研究機構 Epoch AI 估計，截至 2025 年底，Google 擁有全球約 25\% AI 算力，是最大持有者，業界專家與媒體報導愈來愈傾向認為，Google 無法登頂的原因不是算力不足，而是公司資源爭奪：對外銷售算力賺錢的雲端部門、搜尋部門與負責 AI 開發的 DeepMind 仍有激烈的「晶片爭奪戰」情結。

半導體與 AI 基礎設施研究公司 SemiAnalysis 創辦人兼執行長 Dylan Patel，9 日上線的 Big Technology Podcast 表示，Google 過去半年自家模型訓練與推論用算力占比，低於兩三年前。Google 整體算力逐年大增，但分配給 Google DeepMind 的部分成長有限，比例反而下降。他把這個局面比喻為 Google Cloud 負責人庫里安（Thomas Kurian）與 DeepMind 共同創辦人哈薩比斯（Demis Hassabis）之間的競爭，形容「庫里安贏了、哈薩比斯輸了」；文章並提到哈薩比斯更於 8 月退出經營第一線。

Dylan Patel 預測，若只比較 DeepMind、Anthropic 與 OpenAI 三家，到 2026 年底 DeepMind 的算力最少。2027 年差距可能更擴大：OpenAI 與 Anthropic 2027 年將各自增加 5\~10GW 資料中心容量，若 Google 為自家用途只增加數 GW，雙方差距會再拉開。文章結論是，將算力賣給競爭對手比自己用更賺錢，這個經營現實與組織力學的扭曲，是 Google 坐擁最多算力卻拿不到 AI 模型首位的背景。

Google.title: Gemini 4 Argon Arrives With Big Claims for AI Agents and Scientific Discovery - AIwire
Google.description: Google just released the new Gemini 4 Argon, which it claims can generate up to a million tokens in a single run, a big jump for long code migrations and multi-step agent work. Competitors top out around 128 ... With Gemini 4 Argon, Google has also made a big push toward unlocking new scientific breakthroughs.
Google.content:
## Off the Wire Press Releases

by Ali Azhar | October 21, 2026

Google just released the new Gemini 4 Argon, which it claims can generate up to a million tokens in a single run, a big jump for long code migrations and multi-step agent work. Competitors top out around 128,000 output tokens per request, so based on that claim, Argon’s 1 million is roughly 8x higher.

Argon is now available globally, with developers accessing it through the paid Gemini API and businesses through Google Cloud. Individual users need a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, while access to the version without cybersecurity restrictions requires separate approval. Argon costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30. Both rates double in December.

Google says it is also its most resilient model yet. It is built to withstand indirect prompt injection. That is the kind of attack that could hijack an AI agent working inside a company. Independent testing of that claim has not been shared by Google.

Argon is built on a sparse mixture-of-experts design, which routes each input to a small set of specialized sub-networks. This is the opposite approach to running the whole model at once. It’s worth keeping in mind that this is a new model, not a fine-tune of an earlier one.

Unlike rivals such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, which list text and image input, Argon can also take audio and video, though it only produces text. Paired with code execution, search grounding and function calling, that makes it a candidate for AI agents that work through multi-step tasks.

Google also shared some interesting benchmark results. Argon scored 68.9% on Vals Index. This was a lead against rivals GPT-6 Astra (63.1%) and Claude Opus 5.5 (67%). The Vals Index is designed to test models on the kind of work people do in finance, law, coding and tax services.

Argon also scored 51.3% on AutomationBench, beating both rivals again. The AutomationBench tests whether AI agents can actually complete tasks across different business applications. However, 51.3% by itself isn’t exactly a high success rate. What this means is that nearly half the tasks still went unfinished or were done incorrectly. Compared to rivals this might be good, but it raises concerns about the overall ability of the tested models. All these figures are based on Google’s published comparisons.

Google has also been using Argon internally. The Chrome team put it to work on hundreds of files in Chromium, the codebase behind Chrome. Google says the changes were done in weeks, rather than the months they would normally have taken. Its Agent Development Kit team found improvements too, with session preparation time dropping 40% and cold imports getting 21% faster.

Gopal Srinivasan, Global AI and Data Lead, Deloitte, has also been impressed with the model. He said, “Early impressions from Gemini 4 are very strong: for long-running tasks across these workflows, it completed successfully 100% of the time in our evals, maintaining context and running through multiple tools across impressive spans.

“Its depth of reasoning delivers significantly higher, clearer output. Performing in-depth reasoning for domain-specific tasks without detailed prior logic or instructions is something we’ve never seen with any model in its class before.”

With Gemini 4 Argon, Google has also made a big push toward unlocking new scientific breakthroughs. The company shared that “Argon is already having real-world impact across the scientific community.”

In quantum computing, Argon helped nearly double the inference throughput of Google’s AlphaQubit error-correction system. Another implementation it produced cut the spacetime cost of a quantum operation by more than 100 times compared with an earlier method.

Google researchers also worked with University of Maryland professor Matt Landreman on nuclear fusion. They found new mathematical solutions that could help researchers test simulations of stellarator reactors.

At Gamow Labs, Argon spotted a chromosomal rearrangement in a newborn’s genetic data that conventional software had missed for years. In another experiment, Google used Argon to design five new enzymes in hours. All five showed catalytic activity when tested in the lab.

“Gemini 4 represents a step change in what AI can accomplish in real-world science,” said Alex Cabrera, Founding Engineer, Axiom Bio.

“We’ve seen the reason through complex experimental data, from cellular imaging to mass spectrometry, and make subtle findings that traditionally require expert scientists to identify. On our Scientific Agent Benchmark, Gemini 4 was at the frontier across most tasks, including our hardest: ranking the clinical risk between two drugs.”

Google is offering 10,000 eligible scientists six months of free access to its highest Antigravity usage tier.

Google.description: The way I think about compute allocation is making sure Google DeepMind, both for research and frontier model development, is cutting edge in terms of compute access. ... Nowadays, even on my phone, Gemini voice models are so good. ... a product—the Gemini app I’m talking about. ... One of the exciting things we announced recently is the unified Gemini agent for enterprise, and we’re bringing that to consumers.
Google.content:
Editorial

# Is Google Really Back at the Frontier? Sundar Pichai Tells Us

21 MINUTE READ|Digital ExperienceDigital Experience|Oct 21, 2026

OCT 21, 2026

In a Q&A with Alex Kantrowitz, Pichai tells us about compute trade-offs, safety gaps and the personal agents coming next.

Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has little patience for doubts about Google’s willingness or capacity to compete at the frontier of AI.

His company’s latest Gemini 4 Argon model — long-promised and recently delivered — beats OpenAI and Anthropic’s latest public models on coding, math, science, and knowledge-work benchmarks and has placed Google’s AI back among the world’s best.

Amid chatter that Google was fine with good-enough lightweight ‘Flash’ models, Pichai pushed back hard against any suggestion that company is limiting its research ambitions. “We won’t do it any other way,” he told me in a Big Technology Podcast interview recorded this week at Google’s Mountain View headquarters.

Pursuing cutting-edge research is costly for Google, requiring compute and chips that otherwise could be sold at a high markup by its cloud business. But Pichai said allocating resources to frontier AI development is “ground zero” for Google.

“Our cloud business is at any given moment in time forgoing short-term revenues because we are making compute trade-offs to support frontier AI development,” Pichai told me.

In our conversation, we discussed Argon (which Pichai says processed three times as many tokens as Gemini 3 in the 72 hours after launch), AI’s role in developing better models, the AI interface of the future, competition with OpenAI, Google’s partnerships with Anthropic and Apple, data centers in space, and the nature of his optimism.

## Why Google Is Committed to the AI Frontier

Alex Kantrowitz: Google is back at the frontier with Gemini 4 Argon, which beats OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s public models on benchmarks spanning coding, math, science, and knowledge work.

The conventional wisdom was that Google had given up on the frontier to focus on fast, good-enough models for its products. That was wrong?

Sundar Pichai: Very wrong. Look, we are so committed to being at the frontier. It’s in our DNA. We won’t do it any other way. We’ve been thinking about the AI frontier for well over a decade now.

The frontier is very dynamic. It’s very competitive. It’s very exciting. I couldn’t be more pleased with how Argon has come together. We took our time with it. We made sure we tested it safely and deployed it carefully. We took a bit longer than our other models, given its capabilities.

Across the board, be it for agentic work, knowledge work, coding, creative tasks, Argon is one of the really good frontier models. The first 72 hours since we launched, it’s almost up to 25 trillion tokens used, which is about three times what Gemini 3.0 had in the first 72 hours. And we are capacity constrained as we are serving it.

Excited, but there are always areas….. You know, the frontier is very dynamic, and you have to keep evolving the models. There are areas which we can see we need to improve as well. We’ll be at work on all of that as well.

Which areas?

On any given model, Argon would be across the board better at everything if you just look even two months back. But the space is so evolving. Even on coding, for example, there are pockets where we know we need to do better, and there’s clear feedback. We’ll make it better.

The argument for standard models is that they’re already good enough to build great products, with the frontier valuable only for certain tasks. Meta built Muse with good models rather than the best, and Google could put standard models into Maps, Gmail, and Search. Why isn’t that sufficient?

It’s definitely not how I have thought about it at all. We are deeply committed to driving the state of the art and actually pushing where this technology can go, all the way from transformers. That’s a journey we’ve been on. You will see us continue to do that.

When you’re at the frontier, you get an earlier look into the emerging capabilities, earlier than others, which helps you better prepare for the future. We are fortunate to have a wide set of opportunities across consumer and enterprise. Some of our cloud customers, for sure, want the model at the frontier.

The frontier models will be better at developing the next set of models in an era of recursive self-improvement. I would argue it matters there. Internally, we have definitely seen a steep point of inflection by deploying Argon to our developers. It definitely tackles problems which our previous models could not do. Being at the frontier puts you at the innovation frontier and helps you drive that as well.

There is room for models of all sizes and capabilities. That’s why we did Flash, Flash-Lite, etc. I agree with you that you can develop very good product experiences with not necessarily the most frontier model, because they tend to be slower and more expensive too. But we care about the Pareto frontier, and we’re committed to doing all of that.

You said developing frontier models gives you a look at what’s coming. What do you see on the horizon?

What makes this moment so exciting is you build something which you think is a culmination of months of work, and you put it out. You already see clear headroom ahead.

We’ve all been working on these agentic, long-horizon capabilities, but clearly the frontier is going to have multiple of these agents working together to do things. That’s an example of an exciting paradigm underway.

It’s also clear to me that users, both in consumer and enterprise, will have access to some multi-agent framework for them, working all the time doing things. It feels like a moment of infinite possibilities.

## Self-Improvement and AI Safety

Sergey Brin said one of Argon’s core innovations was relying more on the model to help develop the model. Yet incidents involving OpenAI’s bots breaking containment and Google’s bots accessing a site they shouldn’t have suggest these systems still aren’t perfectly aligned. Isn’t there reasonable cause for concern about accelerating toward recursive self-improvement?

There are three parts to your question. Let’s first talk about RSI itself. You’re right, Sergey mentioned RSI being a critical contributor as we are developing Argon. But to be very clear, today, in a continuum, we are pretty far from the end state of RSI or something like that.

The right way to describe it is you have RSI loops along with AI researchers in various aspects of model development. You almost have agents helping AI researchers in some automated way work together to build these models. It’s good to at least understand where we are today, and it’s super exciting. I expect that continuum to keep making progress as we go into next year.

The second question is around safety. Security comes from defense in depth. You’re talking about alignment, obviously. We all are doing a lot of work to make sure the models are as aligned as possible. But it’s an active area of research, and there are clear gaps.

That’s not the only thing we rely on. You have the work you do on alignment, but beyond that, we put a lot of effort into real-time monitoring as these models are working. Making sure you have good telemetry into what’s happening so that you can intervene in real time if you see unexpected behaviors.

How you do that, the architecture with which you do that, how you make sure it’s all sandboxed and isolated in a way that it can continue doing its job during real-time monitoring — these are all areas of investment.

Obviously, when we deploy these models, giving customers, enterprises, control, both with real-time monitoring, but their ability to decide where they deploy, what type of data which models ever have access to, etc. All that work is very, very important, and we are doing a lot of that.

As an industry, we need to constantly up our game and take the time to do all this stuff, including dedicating the compute required to make sure you can safely deploy these models.

The third part is: Is it all enough? This is why there are a lot of conversations in the industry, and I think it’s reasonable to be worried. The right way to approach something you worry about is early on thinking about what more we can do.

As an industry, you’re definitely seeing increased levels of work on alignment, testing for safety, etc., as we deploy these models. The next step would be developing better standards so there are cross-industry standards of how we do these things, including the ability to evaluate using independent evaluators.

If you look at areas like financial controls, we have accounting standards, we have independent auditors. Those are all the next natural steps for us as an industry to work toward, and regulation will end up playing a role as we go through all of that as well.

Google pursues both language models and world models, while some other AI companies like OpenAI have focused more heavily on LLMs as the path to AGI. Why is world-model research important to you?

As humans, you obviously perceive the world around you, and you’re taking all those inputs. Making sure these models are able to understand the laws of physics, simulate the world in high fidelity. All that, I think, are key enabling blocks for intelligence.

We are working across all possible applications of this. Take an area like robotics. It’s not an accident: If you look at embodied reasoning benchmarks, Argon is state of the art. That all comes from our experience building world models.

Inherently, I would expect there will be architectures which will converge all of this in the future. But for us, we view this as, today, this jagged frontier that is intelligence. We want to be at the frontier of all the possible approaches, and that will help us both drive better research, better insights, and develop a much better AGI model, is how we think about it.

Meta.content:
# Meta forced to identify staff behind Shadow Library downloads for Llama models

In a major development in copyright litigation against big tech, a US federal judge has ordered Meta to disclose the identities of internal employees and researchers who torrented and curated millions of pirated books from shadow libraries to train its Llama artificial intelligence models.

Credit: VCG/VCG via Getty Images

The training regimes powering modern large language models have come under intense legal scrutiny from authors, publishers, and intellectual property holders. In an ongoing class-action lawsuit filed by prominent authors—including Sarah Silverman and Richard Kadrey—plaintiffs allege that Meta unlawfully ingested vast repositories of copyrighted literary works without licensing or compensation. Moving beyond general corporate liability, a US district court judge has granted the plaintiffs' motion to compel, formally ordering Meta to turn over the unredacted names and internal communications of the specific engineers, data curators, and managers responsible for downloading and processing pirated book archives.

Meta has been ordered to name executives who authorized downloading books from shadow libraries such as Anna's Archive and LibGen, TorrentFreak reported. Magistrate Judge Thomas Hixon's discovery order, in AI-training copyright suits by authors including Richard Kadrey and Sarah Silverman and by Entrepreneur Media, also compels Meta to produce command history files for every server it used to torrent. Meta had argued no one with authority decided to torrent. Authors argue Meta also seeded; Meta says it used mitigations to prevent seeding. Meta's defense is that no one with authority chose to torrent, which leaves the servers as the only executives the command history can name. @Meta

— V_L_S_ (@_V_L_S_) October 20, 2026

### Shadow Library allegations: Books3 and LibGen

At the center of the dispute are controversial datasets known in AI research circles as "Books3" and "Library Genesis" (LibGen). Court records and leaked internal chat logs revealed that Meta researchers discussed downloading torrent files containing tens of thousands of contemporary books, acknowledging the ambiguous legal origins of the data while prioritizing training volume to keep pace with rival frontier models from OpenAI and Google DeepMind. While Meta previously attempted to protect employee privacy by redacting individual identifiers from discovery disclosures, the presiding judge ruled that plaintiffs have a legitimate legal right to depose key decision-makers directly.

### Corporate shielding falls: Personal liability and depositions

The ruling pierces the veil of anonymity that tech corporations traditionally maintain during early-stage intellectual property litigation. By forcing Meta to name names, individual engineers and team leads can now be subpoenaed for sworn depositions. Plaintiffs' counsel aims to establish whether management directed staff to bypass copyright laws intentionally, which could establish willful infringement and unlock statutory damages reaching millions of dollars per registered work—sharpening the stakes around how commercial foundation models like Muse Spark Open and Llama architectures are trained.

Uploading Pirated Books via BitTorrent Qualifies as Fair Use, Meta Argues | Ernesto Van der Sar, Torrentfreak In the race to build the most capable LLM models, several tech companies sourced copyrighted content for use as training data, without obtaining permission from content owners. Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, was one of the companies to get sued. In 2023, well-known book authors, including Richard Kadrey, Sarah Silverman, and Christopher Golden, filed a class-action lawsuit against the company. Meta’s Bittersweet Victory Last summer, Meta scored a key victory in this case, as the court concluded that using pirated books to train its Llama LLM qualified as fair use, based on the arguments presented in this case. This was a bittersweet victory, however, as Meta remained on the hook for downloading and sharing the books via BitTorrent. By downloading books from shadow libraries such as Anna’s Archive, Meta relied on BitTorrent transfers. In addition to downloading content, these typically upload data to others as well. According to the authors, this means that Meta was engaged in widespread and direct copyright infringement. In recent months, the lawsuit continued based on this remaining direct copyright infringement claim. While both parties collected additional evidence through the discovery process, it remained unclear what defense Meta would use. Until now. Seeding Pirated Books is Fair Use Last week, Meta served a supplemental interrogatory response at the California federal court, which marks a new direction in its defense. For the first time, the company argued that uploading pirated books to other BitTorrent users during the torrent download process also qualifies as fair use. Meta’s reasoning is straightforward. Anyone who uses BitTorrent to transfer files automatically uploads content to other people, as it is inherent to the protocol. In other words, the uploading wasn’t a choice, it was simply how the technology works. Meta also argued that the BitTorrent sharing was a necessity to get the valuable (but pirated) data. In the case of Anna’s Archive, Meta said, the datasets were only available in bulk through torrent downloads, making BitTorrent the only practical option. “Meta used BitTorrent because it was a more efficient and reliable means of obtaining the datasets, and in the case of Anna’s Archive, those datasets were only available in bulk through torrent downloads,” Meta’s attorney writes. “Accordingly, to the extent Plaintiffs can come forth with evidence that their works or portions thereof were theoretically ‘made available’ to others on the BitTorrent network during the torrent download process, this was part-and-parcel of the download of Plaintiffs’ works in furtherance of Meta’s transformative fair use purpose.” In other words, obtaining the millions of books that were needed to engage in the fair use training of its LLM, required the direct downloading, which ultimately serves the same fair use purpose. Authors and Meta Disagree over Fair Use Timing The authors were not happy with last week’s late Friday submission and the new defense. On Monday morning, their lawyers filed a letter with Judge Vince Chhabria flagging the late-night filing as an improper end-run around the discovery deadline. They point out that Meta had been aware of the uploading claims since November 2024, but that it never brought up this fair use defense in the past, not even when the court asked about it. The letter specifically mentions that while Meta has a “continuing duty” to supplement discovery under Rule 26(e), this rule does not create a “loophole” allowing a party to add new defenses to its advantage after a court deadline has passed. “Meta (for understandable reasons) never once suggested it would assert a fair use defense to the uploading-based claims, including after this Court raised the issue with Meta last November,” the lawyers write. Meta’s legal team fired back the following day, filing their own letter with Judge Chhabria. This letter explains that the fair use argument for the direct copyright infringement claim is not new at all. Meta pointed to the parties’ joint December 2025 case management statement, in which it had explicitly flagged the defense, and noted that the author’s own attorney had addressed it at a court hearing days later. “In short, Plaintiffs’ assertion that Meta ‘never once suggested it would assert a fair use defense to the uploading-based claims, including after’ the November 2025 hearing, is false” Meta’s attorney writes in the letter. Authors Admit No Harm, No Infringing Output Meanwhile, it’s worth noting that Meta’s interrogatory response also cites deposition testimony from the authors themselves, using their own words to bolster its fair use defense. The company notes that every named author has admitted they are unaware of any Meta model output that replicates content from their books. Sarah Silverman, when asked whether it mattered if Meta’s models never output language from her book, testified that “It doesn’t matter at all.” Meta argues these admissions undercut any theory of market harm. If the authors themselves cannot point to infringing output or lost sales, the lawsuit is less about protecting their books and more about challenging the training process itself, which the court already ruled was fair use. These admissions were central to Meta’s fair use defense on the training claims, which Meta won last summer. Whether they carry the same weight in the remaining BitTorrent distribution dispute has yet to be seen. ‘U.S. AI Leadership at Stake’ In its interrogatory response, Meta added further weight by stressing that its investment in AI has helped the U.S. to establish U.S. global leadership, putting the country ahead of geopolitical competitors. That’s a valuable asset worth treasuring, it indirectly suggested. As the case moves forward, Judge Chhabria will have to decide whether to allow this “fair use by technical necessity” defense. Needless to say, this will be of vital importance to this and many other AI lawsuits, where the use of shadow libraries is at stake. For now, the BitTorrent distribution claims remain the last live piece of a lawsuit filed in 2023. Whether Judge Chhabria will allow Meta’s new defense to proceed has yet to be seen. Read more: https://t.co/y1A9oRrGKy

— Owen Gregorian (@OwenGregorian) March 8, 2026

### Industry-wide ramifications for AI training data

Legal analysts describe the decision as a watershed moment for the generative AI sector. For years, foundational model developers treated web scraping and shadow torrents as industry-standard research methods protected under the fair use doctrine

# Llama 4

## 1. Model Introduction
Llama 4 is Meta’s latest generation of open-source LLM model with industry-leading performance. SGLang has supported Llama 4 Scout (109B) and Llama 4 Maverick (400B) since v0.4.5. Ongoing optimizations are tracked in the Roadmap. This generation delivers comprehensive upgrades across the board: The highly capable Llama 4 Maverick with 17B active parameters out of ~400B total, with 128 experts. The efficient Llama 4 Scout also has 17B active parameters out of ~109B total, using just 16 experts. Both models leverage early fusion for native multimodality, enabling them to process text and image inputs. Maverick and Scout are both trained on up to 40 trillion tokens on data encompassing 200 languages (with specific fine-tuning support for 12 languages including Arabic, Spanish, German, and Hindi). For more details, please refer to the official llama4 Repository:https://www.llama.com/models/llama-4/

## 2. SGLang Installation
SGLang offers multiple installation methods. You can choose the most suitable installation method based on your hardware platform and requirements. Please refer to the official SGLang installation guide for installation instructions. For SGLang CPU installation, please refer to the CPU version installation guide.

## 3. Model Deployment
This section provides a progressive guide from quick deployment to performance optimization, suitable for users at different levels.

### 3.1 Basic Configuration
Interactive Command Generator: Use the configuration selector below to automatically generate the appropriate deployment command for your hardware platform, model variant, deployment strategy, and thinking capabilities.
