cross_cutting.content:
# Vultr and AMD Expand Global Collaboration with New AI Infrastructure in India

21 Oct 2026

## New Chennai deployment will create one of the world’s largest AMD Instinct™ superclusters, expanding AI compute access in India

Vultr, the world’s largest privately-held cloud infrastructure company, today announced a major expansion of its AMD powered infrastructure for enterprise and sovereign cloud initiatives. Vultr will deploy AMD Instinct™ MI355X GPUs in a new 20 MW supercluster in Chennai, India, creating the country’s largest AMD Instinct deployment and giving Vultr two of the world’s largest AMD AI infrastructure deployments globally, alongside its flagship supercluster in Springfield, Ohio. With 288GB of HBM3E memory and 8TB/s of memory bandwidth per GPU, AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs provide the performance and memory capacity required to develop and deploy increasingly complex AI models at scale.

The Chennai supercluster is designed to serve AI labs and foundation model builders, AI-native startups, enterprises, and research and academic institutions. It will support demanding AI workloads including large language model and foundation model training, fine-tuning and high-throughput inference, providing the compute capacity organizations need to develop and deploy AI at scale.

“Enterprises deploying AI at scale need infrastructure they can access locally to meet data sovereignty, data residency, and latency requirements,” said J.J. Kardwell, CEO of Vultr. “Vultr’s Chennai supercluster, powered by AMD MI355X GPUs, gives organizations in India the capacity to train, fine-tune, and run inference on in-country infrastructure.”

Vultr’s longstanding relationship with AMD spans the AMD Instinct GPU roadmap, from MI300X and MI325X to MI355X and the planned MI455X and AMD Helios rack-scale architecture, together with the AMD EPYC data center CPUs that power Vultr VX1 Cloud Compute. The Chennai deployment extends that collaboration as AMD and Vultr expand access to advanced AI infrastructure through Vultr’s global cloud footprint. Looking ahead, Vultr plans significant additional capacity expansion in 2027, including AMD Instinct™ MI455X GPUs and the AMD Helios™ rack-scale AI architecture, broadening global access to next-generation AI infrastructure.

The Chennai supercluster will also leverage the AMD ROCm™ open software ecosystem, giving developers access to widely used AI frameworks, libraries and models, with greater flexibility and choice in how they develop and deploy AI workloads. The open software approach also supports AI innovation in India through open-source software and community-driven development.

“India has the talent and ideas to build the next generation of AI. Access to compute at this scale will help turn more of those ideas into reality , ” said Jaya Jagadish, Country Head & SVP Engineering, AMD India. “Through our collaboration with Vultr, we’re expanding access to AMD Instinct compute in India, backed by the AMD ROCm open software ecosystem, giving researchers, startups and enterprises greater choice and flexibility in how they develop and deploy AI.”

The launch comes as demand for sovereign cloud infrastructure is rising globally. Security concerns, regulatory requirements and performance expectations are intensifying the need for in-country infrastructure that can support advanced AI workloads. With 34 global cloud data center regions, Vultr provides secure, compliant infrastructure at a predictable cost to enterprises, AI innovators, and government agencies in 17 countries across six continents. The Chennai deployment reflects a broader shift toward geographically-distributed AI infrastructure, bringing large-scale compute closer to where data is created and AI applications are deployed.

To learn more about Vultr’s collaboration with AMD, visit www.vultr.com/cloudalliance/amd/ or contact sales to get started.

About Vultr

Vultr is on a mission to make high-performance cloud infrastructure easy to use, affordable, and locally accessible for enterprises and AI innovators around the world. Vultr is trusted by hundreds of thousands of active customers across 185 countries for its flexible, scalable, global Cloud Compute, Cloud GPU, Bare Metal, and Cloud Storage solutions. In December 2024 Vultr announced an equity financing at a $3.5 billion valuation. Founded by David Aninowsky and self-funded for over a decade, Vultr has grown to become the world’s largest privately-held cloud infrastructure company.

Learn more at: www.vultr.com .

cross_cutting.content:
# Armada, Johnson Controls plan 500MW AI infrastructure rollout

#### Author: Joe Peck

Armada, a US provider of modular edge data centres and connectivity for remote sites, plans to work with Johnson Controls, a global provider of smart building technologies, to build 500MW of distributed sovereign super intelligence (SI) infrastructure in 2027, using factory-integrated systems based on NVIDIA’s DSX POD reference design and Vera Rubin platform.

Announced at NVIDIA GTC, the collaboration will combine engineering, manufacturing, and deployment to deliver modular infrastructure with cabling, wiring, piping, and functional validation completed before shipment.

## Factory-built infrastructure aims to accelerate deployment

The NVIDIA DSX POD reference design moves repeatable construction work from data centre sites into factories. Compute, networking, rack-level power, plumbing for liquid cooling, and supporting infrastructure are integrated and validated before delivery.

On site, the containers are connected to prepared power, water, cooling, and networking infrastructure, with capacity expanded by adding standardised units.

Armada will use NVIDIA DSX Air to simulate AI factories and validate its Bridge GPU management software before shipment. Once deployed, NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS will help manage power and workloads to maximise computing throughput within each site’s available power capacity.

Dan Wright, co-founder and CEO of Armada, says, “The SI race isn’t going to be won by whoever pours concrete the fastest. Companies and nations can have the chips, the land, the power, and the ambition and still be told to wait years for a building.

“The NVIDIA DSX POD reference design lets us cut that wait out of the equation. We build the SI factory in one of our Galleon Forge factories, ship it, connect it, and our customers are generating tokens in months on infrastructure they own and control.”

## Distributed capacity for sovereign AI

Armada says conventional 50MW facilities can take years to become IT-ready and require around 600,000 on-site labour hours. It also cites a projected construction workforce shortfall of 288,000 workers by 2027 as a challenge to expanding capacity.

The company plans to deploy modular SI facilities close to energy sources, including stranded, renewable, and off-peak power. Its proposed architecture is designed to operate without cloud dependencies, allowing customers to retain control of their models, data, and infrastructure.

Charlie Boyle, Vice President of DGX Systems at NVIDIA, notes, “The demand for compute is outpacing the speed at which the world can build the facilities to house it.

“By utilising the NVIDIA DSX POD reference design, Armada can deliver factory-built, Vera Rubin-based containers to customers. Together with Johnson Controls, Armada is positioned to bring Vera Rubin-based factories to customers who need capacity now, wherever their energy and data are.”

## Manufacturing partnership

Armada brings experience deploying modular data centre infrastructure in remote and challenging environments, including Alaska, a US Navy littoral combat ship, and desert locations in the Middle East.

The company says its manufacturing and deployment capabilities will support the planned rollout, with Johnson Controls contributing thermal management technology, engineering, and global manufacturing capacity.

Joakim Weidemanis, CEO of Johnson Controls, comments, “NVIDIA is rapidly advancing the age of intelligence and reshaping the infrastructure required to support it.

“Our collaboration with Armada combines their expertise in deploying compute at the edge with Johnson Controls’ advanced thermal management technology, engineering capabilities, and global manufacturing scale. This combination delivers high-performance infrastructure engineered to quickly bring capacity online where and when it’s needed.”

Under the collaboration, NVIDIA will design, test, and validate the DSX POD reference design for the Vera Rubin platform, whilst Armada will engineer, manufacture, integrate, customise, service, and deliver the modular data centres.

cross_cutting.content:
# Nvidia plans sovereign AI factories with European telecom operators

Nvidia is collaborating with European telecom operators to set up AI factories that enhance local infrastructure. Around ten telecom companies in EMEA are set to adopt Nvidia's advanced computing hardware for various AI applications. Deutsche Telekom plans to expand its industrial AI cloud platform using Nvidia's technology for physical applications. Elisa has successfully conducted a pioneering AI-RAN trial integrating multiple services on Nvidia's platform.

Nvidia plans to help European telecom operators establish sovereign AI factories, marking an expansion into the telecom sector, SDxCentral reported on Wednesday.

The company confirmed at its GTC event in Berlin that approximately 10 telecom operators in EMEA have committed to using its accelerated computing hardware. This hardware will power various applications, including industrial AI clouds and AI-RAN.

Ian Buck, Nvidia's VP and GM for hyperscale and high-performance computing, stated in a press briefing that this represents a "new path to market." This path aims to expand AI infrastructure and services across Europe.

Nvidia has already invested $1 billion in Nokia. Companies like Deutsche Telekom, BT, and Orange have trialed GPU-accelerated platforms or hosted Nemotron open models. This aims to unlock new business models through AI.

Buck noted that telecom companies own about 20 per cent of Europe's data centres. This number rises to over 1,500 when including edge sites.

Nvidia argues that telecom operators are well-suited to support sovereign infrastructure. They already own data centres, regional sites, and cell sites with power, fibre, and spectrum.

Deutsche Telekom plans to expand its Nvidia-powered industrial AI cloud platform. This platform hosts open models for physical AI applications such as robotics. The carrier is utilising Nvidia's Arc server lines, including the Blackwell-based RTX Pro 6000, for inference between devices and the network edge.

Orange has introduced new voice intelligence services for enterprises and emergency responders. Finnish telecom Elisa conducted Europe's first field trial of AI-RAN with Nvidia over 5G. This trial ran voice, mobile data, and vision AI on a single accelerated computing platform.

Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges commented on integrating AI where it makes a real difference. He highlighted bringing intelligence closer to high-tech industries. Höttges added that companies perform best with optimal networks and smart AI. He said that together with Nvidia, they are making this happen.

cross_cutting.content:
# NVIDIA Cloud Partners Expand European AI Infrastructure

Darius Baruo Oct 21, 2026 15:12 UTC

0 Min Read

NVIDIA said on 21 October 2026 that its cloud partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa and Central Asia are expanding AI infrastructure to support training, inference and agentic applications closer to data and users. The company framed the push as a mix of sovereign compute, open-model services and new controls for AI agents, with the stated aim of giving developers more choice over where workloads run and what software systems are allowed to access.

## Evidence and context

In the company’s announcement published on 21 October 2026, NVIDIA said European AI clouds are adding regional compute capacity and full-stack infrastructure based on its DSX platform, Vera Rubin systems, BlueField DPUs and Spectrum-X networking. NVIDIA said the effort is intended to help developers build agentic and physical AI applications while keeping data and workloads under regional control. The company also said partners are expanding across multiple geographies, but inclusion in the ecosystem does not by itself establish a new country-specific deployment or facility.

NVIDIA said Nscale used the DSX platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements and, in tests using GB300 NVL72 systems, said DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget. NVIDIA also said Nscale plans to deploy Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads and to expand across five European markets.

Other named developments included Crusoe’s liquid-cooled modular AI factories for the Vera Rubin platform; Nebius’ use of NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX with Spectrum-X networking on Nebius Token Factory; Baseten’s model for code-review routing using Nemotron 3.5 Lightning; and Fireworks’ partnership with Era4 to combine model services with direct liquid-cooled capacity powered by Blackwell Ultra GPUs at Era4’s Chesterfield facility. NVIDIA also said Mistral trained Mistral Large 4 on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral-operated European data centers, and that Verda plans to deploy Vera Rubin while using Nemotron, Cosmos and the Dynamo open-source framework.

The announcement also highlighted an OpenShell Reference Architecture for secure agent deployment. NVIDIA said the architecture, announced at GTC Berlin, uses Vera Rubin NVL72 for model inference, Vera CPUs with OpenShell for agent harnesses and tool use, and BlueField-4 DPUs running Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. NVIDIA said partners including Aleria, Baseten, Cassava, CoreWeave, Crusoe, DigitalOcean, Firebird, Fireworks, Firmus, G42, GMI Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Lightning AI, Nebius, Nscale, Radiant, Verda and Vultr are supporting the reference architecture.

The broader backdrop is NVIDIA’s ongoing European infrastructure push. Background material supplied with the announcement notes that on 11 June 2025 NVIDIA outlined European infrastructure plans including 14,000 Blackwell GPUs through UK cloud partners Nebius and Nscale, an initial 18,000 Grace Blackwell systems for Mistral AI in France, and 10,000 Blackwell GPUs for an industrial AI cloud in Germany. Those figures were presented as plans announced on that date, not independently verified installed capacity as of 21 October 2026.

NVIDIA shares last traded at $216.47 as of 21 October 2026 at 10:37:47 UTC, according to the market data provided.

cross_cutting.content:
# SoftBank, Nokia target 2027 for commercial AI-RAN trial in Japan

In a trial planned for 2027, SoftBank and Nokia aim to move AI-RAN out of laboratory environments and validate its performance under real-world, commercial traffic conditions.

Gigi Onag,Senior Editor, APAC,Light Reading

October 22, 2026

3 Min Read

(Source: SOPA Images Limited/Alamy Stock Photo)

Nokia and SoftBank have agreed to conduct a commercial AI-RAN (AI-Radio Access Network) field trial in Japan in 2027. This marks a notable step forward since the trial will take place in a genuine commercial network environment under real commercial traffic conditions, rather than in a controlled lab or isolated testbed setting.

The trial aims to assess the feasibility of running AI and radio network workloads on shared computing infrastructure simultaneously. The two companies essentially want to determine whether the same physical infrastructure used to handle network traffic could also be used to process AI computing tasks, which could improve overall resource utilization and efficiency.

The trial will see Nokia’s AI-native anyRAN Cloud RAN software combined with SoftBank’s AITRAS core AI-RAN platform. The trial will also heavily rely on Nvidia’s Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) platform. The underlying hardware architecture features Nvidia Grace CPUs, Nvidia RTX PRO 4500 GPUs and Nvidia ConnectX-8 networking cards, which can handle heavy AI and radio workloads simultaneously on a single, shared computing infrastructure.

The management of radio and AI resources will be coordinated by integrating the Nokia MantaRay management platform with the AITRAS Orchestrator.

According to SoftBank, not only are telecom networks increasingly required to accommodate growing data traffic, they are also required to provide the computing capabilities needed for low-latency, real-time AI processing as generative AI, AI agents, and physical AI continue to evolve.

The Japanese operator is developing the AITRAS Orchestrator, a platform designed to run AI and RAN workloads on shared infrastructure. In real time, it will monitor demand for computing resources used for AI processing and RAN control, allocating resources flexibly and dynamically based on factors such as resource availability, application requirements and projected power consumption.

SoftBank said that the field trial will assess the suitability of AITRAS as a common platform for hosting RAN software and AI applications from multiple vendors, without the limitations imposed by a specific RAN software implementation.

"Our field trial with Nokia will mark a significant milestone in moving AI-RAN from concept toward commercialization," Ryuji Wakikawa, SoftBank Corp. senior vice president and CTO, said in a statement. "We will further advance AI-RAN validation toward commercialization and work toward a new era of networks that deliver both connectivity and AI services."

##### Transition toward AI-native network architecture

In a separate statement, Nokia said that its latest agreement with SoftBank builds on their ongoing collaboration in AI-RAN, which is supported by Nvidia’s accelerated computing node.

The Finnish equipment vendor added that the trial will contribute to the wider industry shift toward AI-native network architectures by exploring how operators can introduce new capabilities more quickly and support the development of new AI applications at the network edge.

The trial will explore how AI-RAN could support richer, AI-driven experiences, lower-latency services, and new applications powered by real-time intelligence. Future use cases could include physical AI, immersive digital experiences, robotics and autonomous systems that require close interaction between AI and connectivity.

Pallavi Mahajan, Nokia's chief technology and AI officer, noted that their ongoing collaboration with SoftBank is a stepping stone toward developing the automated, AI-native network architectures required for future 6G networks.

"By bringing AI and RAN workloads onto common, programmable infrastructure, AI-RAN has the potential to unlock new levels of spectral efficiency while providing the distributed intelligence needed to support physical AI," she said. "As the boundaries between network and compute continue to blur, this distributed infrastructure can become a powerful platform for both connectivity and AI."

## About the Author

Senior Editor, APAC, Light Reading

Gigi Onag is Senior Editor, APAC, Light Reading. She has been a technology journalist for more than 15 years, covering various aspects of enterprise IT across Asia-Pacific.

She started with regional IT publications under CMP Asia (now Informa), including Asia Computer Weekly, Intelligent Enterprise Asia and Network Computing Asia and Teledotcom Asia. This was followed by stints with Computerworld Hong Kong and sister publications FutureIoT and FutureCIO. She had contributed articles to South China Morning Post, TechTarget and PC Market among others.

She interspersed her career as a technology editor with a brief sojourn into public relations before returning to journalism, joining the editorial team of Mix Magazine, a MICE publication and its sister publication Business Traveller Asia Pacific.

Gigi is based in Hong Kong and is keen to delve deeper into the region’s wide wild world of telecoms.
